notes.text: Read 2026-11-20. There is no separate author page heading; the lighter footer reads 42. The page continues reconstruction of G and f from G-prime and the selected arcs. Diagram (51) displays the claimed passage to the quotient. The following text describes G as a quotient and an amalgamated sum, with (52) explicitly labelled cocart. The final paragraph states a universal property for morphisms taking the complementary arcs to identities. The inserted G dans un and the following G-prime are preserved in their written order without correcting their apparent roles. This is a reading summary, not an independent proof verification.

The first inline map is labelled sigma_G, while the top edge of (51) is plainly labelled o_{G-prime}; the intervening inline label is retraced and is left uncertain. These local forms are preserved instead of enforcing one expected notation. The lower-left capital in (52) is likewise not resolved from the surrounding argument. The struck caption word and its initial-parenthesis/capital-G ambiguity remain doubtful.

The lower horizontal edge of (52) has two visible shaft traces converging on one head. The draft reproduces that double-shaft graphic with the TikZ Rightarrow style; this is a visual transcription decision, not a claim about a distinct categorical meaning. The gathered caption is top-aligned so that the lower-right G stays on the same level as the lower-left S expression. This alignment adjustment is formatting only.

H’s notes explicitly report the formula numbers 51/52, cocart and the caption, so their placement in editorial prose is not counted as omission of those readings. Tilde widths, thin spaces, arrow-label quoting, row separation and gathered wrappers are syntax only. All saved crops were visually inspected; no OCR, external lookup or TeX compilation was used.

main_review_note: The main reader inspected all eleven crops and the original sheet. The opening sigma has an extended top stroke, unlike the round o in (51); the intervening retraced label remains uncertain. The graph primes and low dots are distinct. The two lower-edge shafts in (52) are visibly separated for much of their length and meet one head, so the graphic is retained without a claim about its mathematical meaning. Relative letter heights and the shared component-set notation support the small pi-zero forms; no capital-Pi regularization is imposed. Main review did not confirm the first reader’s certainty on plus: the tall initial and following short strokes also permit bien, so M0999 remains undecided. The apparent exchange of G and G-prime in the final universal-property sentence is preserved as written.
